targetTransferDisposition.closure: No third-Attack, adjacency, target-direction, card-subset, payoff, carrier, cohort, policy or method rescue is permitted.

discoveryEvidence.finding: The death-disambiguation control rejected targetIdx-only as a material alias and exposed 232 forced-death-change turns. This is discovery evidence for a distinct death-produced relay question, not evidence that such a relay is causal or admissible.
discoveryEvidence.reaperBellBoundary: The immutable Reaper Bell family required acquiring a relic and paid immediate Energy plus draw on any non-final death. A direct-kill-to-next-card Dusk relay would instead use no reward acquisition, require an attributable single-target kill and a specific next single-target Attack consumer, and apply one fixed bounded damage operation. An explicit alias audit must pass before implementation.
discoveryEvidence.method: Deterministic exact enumeration remains selected. ML, RL and optimisation remain unauthorised because no policy-repertoire bottleneck with measured method decision value exists.

nextQuestion: Within the 232 discovery-stage forced-death changes, does a preregistered direct attribution predicate identify a reliable, viable, selective and functionally separated Dusk kill relay in which a single-target Attack kills its selected target before any later PLAY and the next PLAY is a single-target Attack against another living enemy in the same turn?
nextAction: Freeze and execute exactly one zero-new-row causal-attribution and alias audit over the complete identity-proved target/death trace. Only complete success may authorise an exact-null and direct-mediator research prototype; the existing target-transfer and Reaper Bell families remain closed.
